user:
QUESTION: Why do chromatin conformation capture (3C) techniques not show which contacts occur in an individual cell at a given time?

ATOM: Chromatin conformation capture (3C) and related techniques usually investigate several thousands to millions of cells, so only population averages of contacts are observed.
KEY POINTS:
1. 3C and related techniques analyze a large number of cells (thousands to millions)
2. Therefore only population averages of contacts are observed

ANSWER TO GRADE:
Because 3C-based methods are population-averaged assays: they crosslink and lyse millions of cells together, so the ligation products reflect the frequency of each contact summed across the whole population rather than the specific set of contacts present in any single cell at one moment. Thus they reveal average contact probabilities, not the heterogeneous, cell-to-cell configurations of chromatin.
